# Continuation Reality — Awtsmoos Studio Completion

> The Awtsmoos makes the next instant new; evidence decides which vessel is true.  
> Awtsmoos.com will not call a painted shell a movie tool while time and frames remain uncoupled from the whole.

## Observed Reality

- The canonical shared movie ecosystem now exists under `apps/shared/movie` and `libs/awtsmoos-movie-core`.
- Awtsmoos Procedural Core now contains `core/movieAssets` plus the procedural movie gateway written in the previous pass.
- `apps/awtsmoos-studio` exists and uses the new `libs/AwtsmoosUI` declarative UI library.
- The current Studio bridge still imports `awtsmoos-movie-core` directly rather than the procedural movie gateway.
- The current Studio viewport is decorative DOM/CSS. It does not execute the shared Canvas movie runtime.
- The current Play button only toggles `playing`; no requestAnimationFrame playback clock advances `playhead`.
- The canonical shared three-minute movie is exactly 180 seconds across 18 ten-second scenes and asserts world3d, light3d, model3d, shapes, paths, charts, 2D/3D particles, 2D/3D characters, text, overlays, and six-plus camera kinds.
- A historical proof MP4 exists, but `ffprobe` measures only 63.833333 seconds, so it fails the requested three-minute acceptance gate.
- A canonical browser proof server and blob receiver are currently running. Chrome has an older `durationMs=180000` target and a fresh `durationMs=30000` stability target owned by another render session. Do not interfere with their leased browser targets.
- `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are installed locally.
- Existing Animator and Mitzvah trees are heavily dirty; new adapter/integration files are safer than broad rewrites.

## Completion Mission

Turn Awtsmoos Studio into a real mobile-first movie authoring/player surface, make its movie bridge go through procedural core, verify the five known studio personalities, add the missing Slides adapter if still absent, run all relevant tests, browser-test desktop/mobile, and produce/probe a genuine current 180-second media artifact.
